claim: The High Court of American Samoa has held that birth certificates should only be altered to correct information that was erroneous at the time of recordation or to reflect a name change due to adoption. Samoa has a large transgender or "third gender" community called fa'afafine, with fa'afatama described as people assigned female at birth who embody both gender traits. Fa'afafine are assigned male at birth and explicitly embody both gender traits ranging from extravagantly feminine to conventionally masculine, recognised as a gender identity/gender role since at least the early 20th century.
